newsitem.title: CROATIA: CROATIA OTC STOCKS CONTINUE TO CLIMB, TRADE SLOWER.
newsitem.headline: CROATIA OTC STOCKS CONTINUE TO CLIMB, TRADE SLOWER.

text.p: Croatian stocks traded on an over-the-counter market continued to climb in the week to August 8 though trade slowed down, the Varazdin Securities Market reported on Monday.
The leading seven-stock VIN index added 1.35 percent to 9,930 points as 16 traded issues rose against three that fell on a weekly basis.
But volume fell to 17,930 from 28,977 shares as the summer lull began to set in, with turnover shrinking to 6.4 from 11.1 million kuna.
Ericsson Nikola Tesla, a Croatian subsidiary of Sweden's Ericsson, again dominated trade with 3,809 units sold and one third of the market's total turnover.
Its stock rose 9.48 percent to end at 635 kuna after peaking at 640 kuna earlier in the week, and was dubbed the current OTC market favourite by traders.
However, due to internal regulations which require each share transfer to be approved by the company board, Tesla cannot trade on the central bourse in Zagreb.
Top gainer was recently overhauled Rijecka Banka, advancing 56.25 percent to 125 kuna on volume of 150 units.
It was followed by hotelier Riviera which added 12.50 percent to 180 kuna with 2,544 shares sold. It closed the week at 188 kuna on the Zagreb Stock Exchange.
Food processor Podravka, which also made a significant recovery in Zagreb, rose 7.55 percent to 285 kuna on volume of 3,603.
The Adriatic pipeline operator Janaf led decliners, losing 7.72 percent to 5,675 in a single deal with five shares.

Shares in brewery Karlovacka Pivovara, in which Chile's Cervecerias has majority, were also on the losing streak as buying subsided slightly. They closed 0.17 percent weaker at 601 kuna, compared to 630 in Zagreb.
Daily OTC closing results are available on page OTCVAR each afternoon Monday-Friday. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
